title: The Rise of Qusayy and the Lineage of the Prophet ﷺ
overview: This episode details how the leadership of Makkah transitioned from the tribe of Khuza'ah back to the descendants of Ismail through the rise of Qusayy ibn Kilab. It describes the establishment of the Quraysh as the custodians of the Ka'bah, the institution of Dar al-Nadwah, and the noble lineage leading to the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.
lessons: The importance of resolving conflict through negotiation and wise arbitration rather than bloodshed.
Leadership in the Islamic tradition is tied to service (khidmah) and hospitality toward others.
An individual's status should be built on noble characteristics and personal integrity rather than inherited position alone.
True honor (izzah) is found in taqwa (God-consciousness) and piety, as physical symbols of power are fleeting.
The fulfillment of oaths and contracts is a hallmark of noble character, even among the people of the Jahiliyyah.
Sacrificing material wealth (like Hakim ibn Hizam's sale) for the sake of Allah reflects a superior understanding of value.

chapters.title: The Early History of Makkah and the Loss of Zamzam
chapters.summary: The lecture begins with a recap of the early settlement of Makkah by Hajar and Ismail, who were joined by the Yemeni tribe of Jurhum. After several centuries of leadership, Jurhum was forcibly ousted by the tribe of Khuza'ah. Before their defeat, Jurhum buried the well of Zamzam to prevent their successors from benefiting from it. During Khuza'ah's rule, Amr ibn Luhayy introduced idol worship and shirk, straying from the original tawhid established by Ibrahim and Ismail.
key_points: The tribe of Jurhum originally settled in Makkah with the permission of Hajar.
Ismail married into the Jurhum tribe, and the Prophet ﷺ is a descendant of this union.
Khuza'ah took control of Makkah by force and ruled for many centuries.
Jurhum buried the well of Zamzam before being displaced from leadership.
Amr ibn Luhayy of Khuza'ah was the first to bring idols into the Arabian Peninsula.

chapters.title: The Rise of Qusayy ibn Kilab
chapters.summary: Qusayy ibn Kilab, a wealthy and highly respected descendant of Ismail from the lineage of Fihr (Quraysh), emerged as a leader. He married the daughter of Hulayl, the ruler of Makkah and leader of Khuza'ah. Upon Hulayl's death, Qusayy proclaimed himself the rightful ruler, asserting that his lineage had the original claim to the city. This led to a violent war between the Quraysh and Khuza'ah, which both sides eventually feared would lead to their mutual extinction.
key_points: Qusayy ibn Kilab was known for his nobility, wealth, and generosity.
Hulayl, the leader of Khuza'ah, gave his daughter in marriage to Qusayy.
Qusayy used the death of his father-in-law as an opportunity to reclaim Makkah's leadership.
Fihr is another name for the progenitor of the Quraysh tribe.
The ensuing conflict between the tribes resulted in heavy casualties on both sides.

chapters.title: The Mediation of Ya'mur ibn 'Awf
chapters.summary: To resolve the bloody conflict, both tribes agreed to accept the arbitration of Ya'mur ibn 'Awf, a wise elder. Qusayy argued that Makkah was the land of his forefather Ismail and that Khuza'ah had no right to hold it by force. Ya'mur ibn 'Awf ruled entirely in favor of Qusayy, granting him the leadership of Makkah and the various custodial rights of the Ka'bah. This decision was accepted by all parties, marking the beginning of Quraysh's undisputed rule in the city.
key_points: Ya'mur ibn 'Awf was a wise mediator respected by both Quraysh and Khuza'ah.
Qusayy presented a historical argument based on the rights of Ismail's descendants.
The speaker compares the Khuza'ah takeover of Jurhum land to the modern Zionist occupation of Palestine.
The ruling gave Qusayy the rights to provide water (Siqayah) and cover the Ka'bah (Kiswah).
The tribe of Khuza'ah honored their oath and surrendered the rule of Makkah without further fighting.

chapters.title: Dar al-Nadwah and the Succession of Qusayy
chapters.summary: Qusayy established Dar al-Nadwah, a function hall that served as the center of Makkan political and social life. It was the venue for council meetings, war declarations, weddings, and coming-of-age ceremonies. As Qusayy aged, he decided to transfer all his powers to his eldest son, 'Abd al-Dar, to elevate his social status, which was lower than that of his brothers. This transition was initially respected by his other sons, including 'Abd Manaf, but led to internal disputes in the following generation.
key_points: Dar al-Nadwah was a council hall built by Qusayy for all major Makkan events.
The hall was later used by Quraysh to plot the assassination of the Prophet ﷺ before the Hijrah.
Qusayy favored 'Abd al-Dar in the inheritance of power to grant him unearned social respect.
'Abd Manaf and his brothers originally accepted their father's decision out of respect.
Ceremonies for young girls starting to wear the 'abayah were held at Dar al-Nadwah.

chapters.title: The Duties of Siqayah and Hospitality
chapters.summary: After 'Abd al-Dar's death, a dispute arose between his sons and their uncles (the sons of 'Abd Manaf) over the city's leadership. They reached a peaceful negotiation to divide the honors: the family of 'Abd al-Dar kept the Kiswah and Dar al-Nadwah, while the family of 'Abd Manaf took over the Siqayah (providing water). Since Zamzam was still buried, they took great pains to import water and mix it with milk or honey for the pilgrims. This responsibility was eventually inherited by Abdul Muttalib, the grandfather of the Prophet ﷺ.
key_points: Negotiations prevented a war between the uncles and nephews of the Quraysh.
The family of 'Abd Manaf took the duty of hospitality extremely seriously.
Pilgrims were served water mixed with laban (yogurt) or honey as a mark of honor.
Water had to be imported from outside Makkah because the Zamzam well was lost.
Abdul Muttalib inherited the duty of Siqayah through the line of 'Abd Manaf.

chapters.title: The Sale of Dar al-Nadwah and True Honor
chapters.summary: The history of Dar al-Nadwah concludes with its eventual sale centuries later. A descendant of 'Abd al-Dar, while intoxicated, sold the hall to Hakim ibn Hizam for a single bottle of wine. Hakim ibn Hizam, who later became a companion of the Prophet ﷺ, eventually sold the property to the Khalifah Mu'awiyah for 100,000 dinars. When Mu'awiyah questioned selling the 'honor of Quraysh,' Hakim replied that true honor lies in taqwa (piety) rather than physical locations, and he donated the entire proceeds to charity.
key_points: Dar al-Nadwah was sold for a bottle of wine during the Pre-Islamic period.
Hakim ibn Hizam became a Muslim and held the property until the reign of Mu'awiyah.
Mu'awiyah purchased the hall for 100,000 dinars.
Hakim ibn Hizam gave the entire amount as Sadaqah in the way of Allah.
The event illustrates the shift from tribal prestige to Islamic piety (taqwa).

chapters.title: Shaybah and the Name 'Abdul Muttalib'
chapters.summary: The episode explores the paternal lineage of the Prophet ﷺ, focusing on the story of his grandfather, Shaybah. Raised by his mother outside Makkah, Shaybah was eventually brought to the city by his uncle, al-Muttalib. Because people mistook him for his uncle's newly purchased slave, he became known as 'Abdul Muttalib' (the slave of al-Muttalib). The lecture concludes with a recitation of the Prophet's ﷺ lineage from Muhammad ibn Abdullah back to Qusayy ibn Kilab, setting the stage for the story of Zamzam's rediscovery.
key_points: The Prophet's ﷺ grandfather's actual given name was Shaybah.
Al-Muttalib was the brother of Hashim and the uncle of Shaybah.
Shaybah chose to return to Makkah to embrace his family's leadership role.
The name 'Abdul Muttalib' was a result of a mistaken assumption by the Makkans.
The lineage: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abdul Muttalib ibn Hashim ibn Abd Manaf ibn Qusayy ibn Kilab.

segments.translit: Bismillāhir-Raḥmānir-Raḥīm. Al-ḥamdu lillāhi Rabbil-ʿālamīn, wa ṣallallāhu wa sallama wa bāraka ʿalā nabiyyinā Muḥammadin wa ʿalā ālihī wa ṣaḥbihī ajmaʿīn. Rabbishraḥ lī ṣadrī wa yassir lī amrī waḥlul ʿuqdatam min lisānī yafqahū qawlī. Allāhumma ʿallimnā mā yanfaʿunā wanfaʿnā bimā ʿallamtanā wa zidnā ʿilmā.

segments.text: [[insha'Allah|إن شاء الله]], today we will go back to some [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] history. The last couple of weeks we were talking about how different religions came into [[Yemen|اليمن]]. We talked about how Judaism and Christianity entered [[Yemen|اليمن]], and last week we talked about how the Persians took over [[Yemen|اليمن]], and how eventually the ruler of [[Yemen|اليمن]], he accepted Islam.

So now we're going to go back, [[insha'Allah|إن شاء الله]], we're going to go back to the history of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], to the time that was a few generations before the birth of [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ. And we're going to talk about some of the ancestors and the forefathers of the Prophet ﷺ, and we're going to talk about the tribe of the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]], and how they got control of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], how they became the leaders of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]].

So as we know from the first lesson a few weeks ago, when [[Ibrahim|إبراهيم]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]] settled his wife [[Hajar|هاجر]] and his son [[Ismail|إسماعيل]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]] in [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], and the well of [[Zamzam|زمزم]] miraculously sprung up in [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] to take care of [[Ismail|إسماعيل]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]] and his mother,
roam around the [[Jazirat al-Arab|بفرة العرب]] looking for places to settle where they had a water supply.

So Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]], He provided the well of [[Zamzam|زمزم]] for [[Ismail|إسماعيل]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]] and his mother [[Hajar|هاجر]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]]. So this tribe that was roaming around, they had come from [[Yemen|اليمن]] and the name of this tribe was [[Jurhum|جرهم]]. They found that [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] was a place that had water.

And when they came to [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] and they saw [[Ismail|إسماعيل]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]] and his mother, they asked for permission to settle in that land. They didn't take it over by force, but they asked for permission. They asked [[Hajar|هاجر]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]] and [[Ismail|إسماعيل]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]]—or they asked [[Hajar|هاجر]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]] because [[Ismail|إسماعيل]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]] was a baby—so they asked her for permission to stay in this land, and that they would give her some money to drink from that well of [[Zamzam|زمزم]], because this was her well. It was for her and her son, and they respected that.

So [[Hajar|هاجر]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]] agreed to this, and that is how the tribe of [[Jurhum|جرهم]] came into [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] and they settled in [[Makkah|مَكَّة]]. Now when [[Ismail|إسماعيل]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]], when he grew up, he married a woman from that tribe as well. So he married a woman from the tribe of [[Jurhum|جرهم]]. So the descendants of [[Ismail|إسماعيل]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]] are descendants of the tribe of [[Jurhum|جرهم]] from the mother's side.

So [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ is descended from [[Ismail|إسماعيل]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]], and he is descended from the tribe of [[Jurhum|جرهم]] from the wife of [[Ismail|إسماعيل]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]]'s side. So [[Jurhum|جرهم]], they were the leaders of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] for a number of years. But then another tribe called [[Khuza'ah|خزاعة]], they took over [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] by force, and they overpowered the tribe of [[Jurhum|جرهم]], and they took over the leadership and the rule of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] by force.

And [[Jurhum|جرهم]] knew that they were going to be defeated, so before the defeat came, before [[Khuza'ah|خزاعة]] took over, [[Jurhum|جرهم]] buried the well of [[Zamzam|زمزم]]. [[Jurhum|جرهم]] buried the well of [[Zamzam|زمزم]] so that [[Khuza'ah|خزاعة]] couldn't take any benefit from it when they took over the land. So the tribe of [[Jurhum|جرهم]], they remained in [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] as residents of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], but the rule was not amongst them anymore. Now the rule came to [[Khuza'ah|خزاعة]], the tribe of [[Khuza'ah|خزاعة]]. And now [[Zamzam|زمزم]] was hidden, or it was buried.
he is the one who actually brought idol worship back into the [[Jazirat al-Arab|بفرة العرب]].

So [[Khuza'ah|خزاعة]], they had control of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] for many centuries. They kept control of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] for many centuries. And the people of [[Jurhum|جرهم]], who originally had the rule of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], they stayed in [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] as residents, and they were always very upset that their rights had been taken away from them and this rule had been forcibly taken away from them by [[Khuza'ah|خزاعة]]. So after a few centuries, there was a man from the children of [[Ismail|إسماعيل]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]], from the descendants of [[Ismail|إسماعيل]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]]—and of course he was from [[Jurhum|جرهم]], because the wife of [[Ismail|إسماعيل]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]] was a woman from [[Jurhum|جرهم]].

So this man, his name was Qusayy ibn Kilab. Qusayy ibn Kilab, and he was from the children of [[Ismail|إسماعيل]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]], from the descendants of [[Ismail|إسماعيل]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]], and he was from the tribe of [[Jurhum|جرهم]]. And he was a very well-respected man. He was very wealthy, he was rich, he was honored, he was very generous, he was known for his noble characteristics. So everybody respected him, even the tribe of [[Khuza'ah|خزاعة]], they respected him as well, even though he was from the people of [[Jurhum|جرهم]].

They respected him so much that the leader of the [[Khuza'ah|خزاعة]] at that time, the leader of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] at that time from [[Khuza'ah|خزاعة]], his name was Hulayl, he gave his daughter in marriage to Qusayy ibn Kilab. He gave his own daughter in marriage to Qusayy ibn Kilab, even though he was not from the tribe of [[Khuza'ah|خزاعة]], rather he was from the tribe of [[Jurhum|جرهم]]. But out of the honor and respect that they had for this man, the leader of [[Khuza'ah|خزاعة]], the [[sayyid|سيد]] of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], the ruler of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], he gave his own daughter to Qusayy ibn Kilab.

So now Qusayy ibn Kilab married the daughter of the ruler, and his respect and his honor amongst the people increased even more. This is a man from the children of [[Ismail|إسماعيل]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]]—that's one point of respect that they have for him. Now he is married to the daughter of the ruler of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]]—that's another point of respect for him. He is a man of honor, a man of respect, a man of generosity, a man who has such noble characteristics. So his respect amongst the people increased, and he became more powerful.

He became more powerful, and he was thinking of a way how he could get the rule of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] back into the hands of [[Jurhum|جرهم]]. And when his father-in-law died, when Hulayl, the leader of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], the leader of the tribe of [[Khuza'ah|خزاعة]], when he died—and he was the father-in-law of Qusayy—when he died, Qusayy proclaimed himself the new ruler of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]]. He saw this as an opportunity to proclaim himself as the new ruler of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]].

So now the people of [[Khuza'ah|خزاعة]], they're saying, "No, no way. The leader has to be from [[Khuza'ah|خزاعة]]. We are the rulers of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], not [[Jurhum|جرهم]]," and Qusayy is from [[Jurhum|جرهم]]. Qusayy declares himself and he proclaims, "I am the new leader of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]]."

And he gets some help from his own tribe. Now Qusayy, we said he is from the children of [[Ismail|إسماعيل]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]], and from the children of [[Ismail|إسماعيل]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]] was a man named Fihr. And Fihr was also known as [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]]. So Qusayy is from the lineage of Fihr, and Fihr is from the lineage of [[Ismail|إسماعيل]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]]. So Qusayy is from the lineage of [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]].
fighting over honor.
So the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]] under [[Qusayy ibn Kilab|قُصَيّ بن كِلَاب]]
start a fight with [[Khuza'ah|خُزَاعَة]] over who gets to rule [[Makkah|مَكَّة]].
And this fight, this war, it became so severe.
And there were so many casualties from both sides,
from the side of [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]], which is the side of [[Jurhum|جُرْهُم]],
and from the side of [[Khuza'ah|خُزَاعَة]] as well. There were so many deaths, so many casualties,
that the people from both sides, they started to get scared.
They said, "Look, if this goes on like this,
then both of these tribes are going to become extinct.
[[Jurhum|جُرْهُم]] will be gone, and [[Khuza'ah|خُزَاعَة]] will also be gone."
So they were afraid.
So they wanted to come up with a solution.
So they decided to start some negotiations.
And with these negotiations, eventually both sides,
the side of [[Qusayy ibn Kilab|قُصَيّ بن كِلَاب]] and the side of [[Khuza'ah|خُزَاعَة]], they agreed
to have a man named [[Ya'mur ibn 'Awf|يَعْمُر بن عَوْف]].
And [[Ya'mur ibn 'Awf|يَعْمُر بن عَوْف]] was an old man, and he was a very wise old man from the Arabs, and he was respected on both sides.
So after the negotiations, both sides agreed
to allow [[Ya'mur ibn 'Awf|يَعْمُر بن عَوْف]] to mediate between them.
And whatever he decides,
they will agree and surrender to his decision,
whatever side he takes.
Whoever's argument he agrees with and allows them to take the rule of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], they will agree to the [[hukm|حُكْم]], to the ruling of this man, [[Ya'mur ibn 'Awf|يَعْمُر بن عَوْف]].
So both sides agreed. Both sides respected him.
So [[Khuza'ah|خُزَاعَة]] and [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]], they both agreed to let [[Ya'mur ibn 'Awf|يَعْمُر بن عَوْف]] mediate between them.
And they took oaths,
and they brought witnesses that "we swear whatever [[Ya'mur ibn 'Awf|يَعْمُر بن عَوْف]] says, we surrender to it completely without question."
Both sides agreed to this.
So now, the mediation begins.
So [[Qusayy ibn Kilab|قُصَيّ بن كِلَاب]],
he starts with his argument in front of [[Ya'mur ibn 'Awf|يَعْمُر بن عَوْف]], the mediator.
And he says, "This was the land of my father [[Ismail|إِسْمَاعِيل]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]].
[[Zamzam|زَمْزَم]] came up for my father [[Ismail|إِسْمَاعِيل]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]].
This was our land,
and [[Khuza'ah|خُزَاعَة]], they took this land by force.
They took this land by force. They stole it from us when it was our right.
And even though this happened centuries ago, that doesn't make it okay."
So to give like a modern-day analogy of what happened to [[Jurhum|جُرْهُم]], it's like what the Zionists have done to the Palestinians' land today.
Right, that's the Palestinians' land, but the Zionists, they took it over by force, and now the Palestinians are still living there, but they have to live under the Zionist rule.
So this is similar to what happened between [[Jurhum|جُرْهُم]] and [[Khuza'ah|خُزَاعَة]].
[[Khuza'ah|خُزَاعَة]] took [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] by force. [[Jurhum|جُرْهُم]] is still living there, but they have to live under the rule of [[Khuza'ah|خُزَاعَة]].
So this is what [[Qusayy ibn Kilab|قُصَيّ بن كِلَاب]] explained to the mediator, [[Ya'mur ibn 'Awf|يَعْمُر بن عَوْف]].
Now when it's [[Khuza'ah|خُزَاعَة]]'s turn to give their argument to the mediator,
what do they have? They have nothing.
Everybody knows that that's the truth. What [[Qusayy ibn Kilab|قُصَيّ بن كِلَاب]] said is the complete truth,
that [[Khuza'ah|خُزَاعَة]] took over that land by force, and they had no right to do so.
So in the end,
[[Ya'mur ibn 'Awf|يَعْمُر بن عَوْف]], being a fair man, being a man of justice,
he says, "My decision is that everything goes to [[Qusayy ibn Kilab|قُصَيّ بن كِلَاب]].
Everything goes to him:
the right to give water to the [[hujjaj|حجاج]], the right to put the cover on the [[Ka'bah|كَعْبَة]], the rule of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] — it goes to [[Qusayy ibn Kilab|قُصَيّ بن كِلَاب]].
And [[Khuza'ah|خُزَاعَة]], you have nothing."
And remember that both sides had agreed and they swore that they would abide by whatever [[Ya'mur ibn 'Awf|يَعْمُر بن عَوْف]] decides.
And they made sure that they kept their end of the bargain. They didn't try to fight it. They accepted it,
and they left the rule of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], and they gave it up to [[Qusayy ibn Kilab|قُصَيّ بن كِلَاب]].
So this is how the rule of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] came back to the descendants of [[Ismail|إبراهيم]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]].

And this is how the rule of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] came to the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]], because [[Qusayy ibn Kilab|قُصَيّ بن كِلَاب]] was from [[Fihr|فِهْر]], and [[Fihr|فِهْر]] is also known as [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]].
So this is how the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]] first got control of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]].
Now [[Qusayy ibn Kilab|قُصَيّ بن كِلَاب]], as the ruler of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] now,
he's the undisputed ruler of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]].
And everybody loves him and everybody respects him. And now with this increased power that he has,
he becomes even more generous in terms of serving the [[hujjaj|حجاج]] and serving his people. And the love that the people have for him in their hearts, it increases.
So one of the things that [[Qusayy ibn Kilab|قُصَيّ بن كِلَاب]] did once he became the ruler of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] is he built
a hall, a function hall, if you will.
And the name of this function hall was called [[Dar al-Nadwah|دَار الندوة]].
And this [[Dar al-Nadwah|دَار الندوة]], this function hall, it was used by the people of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] for all of their important events and all of their important occasions.
Whenever they would need to make a big announcement,
they would make sure that they announce it from the [[Dar al-Nadwah|دَار الندوة]].
If they were going to announce a war, for example, they would announce it from the [[Dar al-Nadwah|دَار الندوة]].
If the leaders of the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]], if they needed to get together to discuss some matter or to consult on some matter, they would get together in the [[Dar al-Nadwah|دَار الندوة]].
Later on, it even became a place where different types of events would take place.
Like any wedding that would take place in [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], it would take place in the [[Dar al-Nadwah|دَار الندوة]].
And the Arabs, they used to also have a type of ceremony when a girl, when a young girl, when she reaches the age where she has to start wearing the [['abayah|عَبَايَة]] or the outer garment,
they would have some type of a ceremony for that as well, and they would do it in the [[Dar al-Nadwah|دَار الندوة]].
So any important event, any occasion, it was all done in the [[Dar al-Nadwah|دَار الندوة]].
So this hall became a very, very important fixture in the city of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]].
And [[Qusayy ibn Kilab|قُصَيّ بن كِلَاب]],
he was a man of great honor, and he was a man that was so highly respected by the people.

So whatever he built and whatever he took care of, the people held that in high regard as well. So the [[Dar al-Nadwah|دَار الندوة]], it became a place that was known for the honor of the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]].
It became a symbol of the honor of the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]].
Now,
[[Dar al-Nadwah|دَار الندوة]], in later years, it was also the place where the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]] gathered together on the night that [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ made his [[Hijrah|هِجْرَة]]
from [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] to [[Madinah|مدينة]].
The leaders of the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]], they got together in that same [[Dar al-Nadwah|دَار الندوة]],
and in that [[Dar al-Nadwah|دَار الندوة]], they plotted how to get rid of [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ.
They plotted the murder of [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ in that same place, in that [[Dar al-Nadwah|دَار الندوة]].
But Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]], as we know, Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] saved [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ from that plot.
All right, so now when [[Qusayy ibn Kilab|قُصَيّ بن كِلَاب]], when he became old, and he knew that his death was approaching,
he started thinking about what to do about his children.
And he had many children. From the children that he had, one of his sons' name was [['Abd Manaf|عَبْد مَنَاف]],
and another one of his sons was named [['Abd al-Dar|عَبْد الدَّار]], and he had other sons as well.
And he saw that all of his sons were highly regarded and respected by the people.
All of his sons had honor, and they had position, and they had status, and everybody respected them, except one son.

One of his sons, nobody really cared about him that much, and he didn't really have much respect amongst the people, and his name was [['Abd al-Dar|عَبْد الدَّار]]. And he was the oldest son of [[Qusayy ibn Kilab|قُصَيّ بن كِلَاب]].
So

[[Qusayy ibn Kilab|قُصَيّ]] decided that "my other sons, you know, they have a position in society, they have this status, they have this honor, they have this respect, but [['Abd al-Dar|عَبْد الدَّار]], he doesn't have anything.
So in order to get him that status and that honor and respect that his brothers have,"
[[Qusayy ibn Kilab|قُصَيّ بن كِلَاب]] said that "after I die, everything,

all of my power, and all of my honor, and all of these things that I do in terms of taking care of the [[Ka'bah|كَعْبَة]] and taking care of the [[hujjaj|حجاج]], all of these responsibilities, I am giving them to [['Abd al-Dar|عَبْد الدَّار]] alone."
And he prevented any of his other sons from having any share in that. So everything went to [['Abd al-Dar|عَبْد الدَّار]].
Now, the sons of [[Qusayy ibn Kilab|قُصَيّ بن كِلَاب]], they respected his decision. They respected the decision of their father, and they didn't try to fight it.

So [['Abd al-Dar|عَبْد الدَّار]], he becomes the ruler. And now he is responsible for taking care of the [[hujjaj|حجاج]], and taking care of the [[Ka'bah|كَعْبَة]], and taking care of the [[Dar al-Nadwah|دَار الندوة]], and taking care of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]].
So now, when [['Abd al-Dar|عَبْد الدَّار]] died...
the sons of [[Abd al-Dar|عَبْد الدَّار]], they wanted to take over from their father. But
the sons of [[Qusayy ibn Kilab|قُصَيّ بن كِلَاب]] who didn't get anything from him,
they thought that they had more right to get that back from their brother now. And they said to the sons of [[Abd al-Dar|عَبْد الدَّار]], to their nephews,
they said, "Look, our father,
he gave everything to your father
because your father, you know, he didn't have much of a position and he didn't have much respect, so he gave it to him for that reason.
And now that he has passed away, and he got whatever the father intended for him, once he got all of that,
he became respected, and he became honored. So our father's intention was fulfilled. Now that your father has passed away,
it is our right to take this back,
because it should have actually come to us in the first place, but we didn't want to fight against our father's wishes.
So we have more right to take this than you."
But the sons of [[Abd al-Dar|عَبْد الدَّار]], they didn't want to hear that. They said, "No, our father had it, now we get to have it."
So a big fight was about to start between
the remaining sons of [[Qusayy ibn Kilab|قُصَيّ بن كِلَاب]] and the sons of [[Abd al-Dar|عَبْد الدَّار]].
There was going to be a big fight between the uncles and the nephews.
But
before it came to fighting, before it came to war,
they were able to come to a negotiation and they were able to come to an agreement
to split the honor, to split the responsibilities
of the [[Ka'bah|كَعْبَة]]
and the other aspects of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]].
So, the family of [[Abd al-Dar|عَبْد الدَّار]], they got the right to
cover the [[Ka'bah|كَعْبَة]], to do the [[Kiswah|كِسْوَة]] of the [[Ka'bah|كَعْبَة]].
And the family of [[Abd Manaf|عَبْد مَنَاف]], who was one of the other sons of [[Qusayy ibn Kilab|قُصَيّ بن كِلَاب]],
the family of [[Abd Manaf|عَبْد مَنَاف]], they got the right to
give drink to the [[hujjaj|حُجَّاج]], when the [[hujjaj|حُجَّاج]] would come to make [[Hajj|حَجّ]],
[[Abd Manaf|عَبْد مَنَاف]] had the responsibility to provide them with drink. So they were able to come to
an agreement where they would share the responsibilities and share these honors of taking care of the city of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]]. And it continued like this for many generations.
And that's why we know that the grandfather of [[Rasulullah|رَسُولُ اللهِ]] ﷺ, [[Abdul-Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]],
he was in charge of
taking care of the drink of water for the [[hujjaj|حُجَّاج]]. Why is that? Because he was from the family of
of [[Abd Manaf|عَبْد مَنَاف]].
And [[Abd Manaf|عَبْد مَنَاف]] was the one who got the responsibility of providing water for the [[hujjaj|حُجَّاج]]. So that remained with his family, and [[Abdul-Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]]
took over when his turn for that came as well.
Now we know
that that water that [[Abd Manaf|عَبْد مَنَاف]] and subsequently his descendants would provide for the [[hujjaj|حُجَّاج]],
at first,
that water was not coming from [[Zamzam|زَمْزَم]].
Because as we said, many years before, just before [[Khuza'ah|خُزَاعَة]] took over [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], the tribe of [[Jurhum|جُرْهُم]], they buried the well of [[Zamzam|زَمْزَم]].
So there was no [[Zamzam|زَمْزَم]] coming out now in [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], it was hidden.
So they would actually, [[Abd Manaf|عَبْد مَنَاف]] and his descendants after him,
they would get water from outside of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]].

They would actually import water into [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] to provide it for the [[hujjaj|حُجَّاج]]. Look at how seriously they took this obligation. That's not an easy thing to do in those days, to bring water from outside and provide it for the [[hujjaj|حُجَّاج]].
Not only that,
but these people were so honorable
that they wouldn't just give them water like that,
plain water. No.
They had to mix this water with some [[laban|لَبَن]]. [[laban|لَبَن]] is like a yogurt type of drink, like you know, lassi.
Anyone from Pakistan and India, you know what that is, right?
And Arabs, you know what [[laban|لَبَن]] is. They would mix the water with [[laban|لَبَن]],
or they would mix it with honey or something,

right, and then give it to the [[hujjaj|حُجَّاج]], just to show their respect and show their honor to the guests of Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سُبْحَانَهُ وَتَعَالَى]]. So this is how seriously they took this responsibility.
And it continued like that for generations, and it came
to the responsibility of [[Abdul-Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]], the grandfather of the Prophet ﷺ as well when his time came.
So that was one of the great honors and responsibilities that the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]] had: taking care of the [[Ka'bah|كَعْبَة]] and taking care of the [[hujjaj|حُجَّاج]].
After that,
a secondary honor that they had, that they also took very seriously, was taking care of the [[Dar al-Nadwah|دَار النَّدْوَة]],
that function hall that [[Qusayy ibn Kilab|قُصَيّ بن كِلَاب]] built. So they felt that was a great responsibility and a great honor for them as well.
And
the [[Dar al-Nadwah|دَار النَّدْوَة]], it
it was agreed that the [[Dar al-Nadwah|دَار النَّدْوَة]] would stay with the family of [[Abd al-Dar|عَبْد الدَّار]].

That the [[Dar al-Nadwah|دَار النَّدْوَة]]'s responsibilities, taking care of it and its ownership, it would stay with the family of [[Abd al-Dar|عَبْد الدَّار]]. And it remained with the family of [[Abd al-Dar|عَبْد الدَّار]] for many years, for many generations.
Until one day,
it was sold by one of the descendants of [[Abd al-Dar|عَبْد الدَّار]]
to a man named [[Hakim ibn Hizam|حَكِيم بن حِزَام]]
[[radiyallahu 'anhu|رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ]]. [[Hakim ibn Hizam|حَكِيم بن حِزَام]], later on, he became a companion of [[Rasulullah|رَسُولُ اللهِ]] ﷺ.
So how did it get sold to [[Hakim ibn Hizam|حَكِيم بن حِزَام]]?
From the family of [[Abd al-Dar|عَبْد الدَّار]],
there was a man who had the key to the [[Dar al-Nadwah|دَار النَّدْوَة]], and he was the owner of it and he had the responsibility of it.
And [[Hakim ibn Hizam|حَكِيم بن حِزَام]] knew this man,
and they used to actually, in the old days, they used to drink alcohol together. They used to drink wine together, [[Hakim ibn Hizam|حَكِيم بن حِزَام]] and
the owner of the [[Dar al-Nadwah|دَار النَّدْوَة]] who was from the descendants of [[Abd al-Dar|عَبْد الدَّار]].
So one day, they were sitting together, they were drinking together, drinking alcohol together,
and the owner of the [[Dar al-Nadwah|دَار النَّدْوَة]], this man from the family of [[Abd al-Dar|عَبْد الدَّار]], he was drunk. He was completely drunk.
And [[Hakim ibn Hizam|حَكِيم بن حِزَام]], he saw this and he saw this as an opportunity to take advantage of him.
So he said to him, "Will you sell the [[Dar al-Nadwah|دَار النَّدْوَة]] to me? Will you sell it to me?"
And he said, "Yeah, sure, I'll sell it to you." He's drunk. "Yeah, I'll sell it to you, no problem."
So then [[Hakim|حَكِيم]] asked him, "Okay, how much?"
And the man says,
"One bottle of wine.
I'll sell it to you for one bottle of wine."
So [[Hakim ibn Hizam|حَكِيم بن حِزَام]] says, "Okay, I'm ready to do it. Let's do it right now." He wanted to do it quickly before the man
becomes sober again.
So he brought witnesses, and they got the contracts drawn up and everything,
and the transaction took place.
And that is how the [[Dar al-Nadwah|دَار النَّدْوَة]] was sold from the family of [[Abd al-Dar|عَبْد الدَّار]] to [[Hakim ibn Hizam|حَكِيم بن حِزَام]]
[[radiyallahu 'anhu|رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ]].

Now [[Hakim ibn Hizam|حَكِيم بن حِزَام]], as we said, later on he became a companion of [[Rasulullah|رَسُولُ اللهِ]] ﷺ, he became a Muslim, and he kept that [[Dar al-Nadwah|دَار النَّدْوَة]]. It was still under his ownership

during the time of [[Rasulullah|رَسُولُ اللهِ]] ﷺ, and then even after [[Rasulullah|رَسُولُ اللهِ]] ﷺ passed away, during the time of the [[khulafa al-rashidin|خُلَفَاء الرَّاشِدِين]], all of them, during the time of [[Abu Bakr|أَبُو بَكْر]], [[Umar|عُمَر]], [[Uthman|عُثْمَان]], [[Ali|عَلِيّ]] [[radiyallahu 'anhum|رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُمْ]], [[Hakim ibn Hizam|حَكِيم بن حِزَام]] was still alive. He lived to a very old age.
Then during the time of [[Mu'awiyah|مُعَاوِيَة]] [[radiyallahu 'anhu|رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ]], when [[Mu'awiyah|مُعَاوِيَة]] was the khalifah,
[[Hakim ibn Hizam|حَكِيم بن حِزَام]] sold
the [[Dar al-Nadwah|دَار النَّدْوَة]].
He sold [[Dar al-Nadwah|دَار النَّدْوَة]] for 100,000 dinars. He sold it for 100,000 dinars. And when [[Mu'awiyah|مُعَاوِيَة]] [[radiyallahu 'anhu|رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ]],
when he heard this, he was actually angry, he was upset.

He was like, "How could you sell the honor of the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]]? The [[Dar al-Nadwah|دَار النَّدْوَة]], this was the honor of the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]], how could you sell the honor of the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]] for 100,000 dinars?"
And then [[Hakim ibn Hizam|حَكِيم بن حِزَام]], he said,
"Honor today is not from the [[Dar al-Nadwah|دَار النَّدْوَة]]. Honor today is with [[taqwa|تَقْوَى]].
As Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سُبْحَانَهُ وَتَعَالَى]] says,
Surely the most honorable amongst you is the one who has the most [[taqwa|تَقْوَى]]. So there is no honor with the [[Dar al-Nadwah|دَار النَّدْوَة]]. The honor is with [[taqwa|تَقْوَى]].
And

I bear witness, and I want you all to witness that that 100,000 dinars that I got from the sale of [[Dar al-Nadwah|دَار النَّدْوَة]], it is [[Sadaqah|صَدَقَة]] in the way of Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سُبْحَانَهُ وَتَعَالَى]]." And he donated, donated it all [[fi sabilillah|فِي سَبِيلِ اللهِ]]. So this is how
[[Hakim ibn Hizam|حَكِيم بن حِزَام]] sold the [[Dar al-Nadwah|دَار النَّدْوَة]].
Now,
as we said, [[Qusayy ibn Kilab|قُصَيّ بن كِلَاب]], he was from [[Fihr|فِهْر]], from the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]].
And [[Abdul-Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] came from his descendants. Now we said [[Qusayy ibn Kilab|قُصَيّ بن كِلَاب]], he had many sons. From those sons was [[Abd Manaf|عَبْد مَنَاف]],
and he also had [[Abd al-Dar|عَبْد الدَّار]], and he had other sons.
Okay, from his son [[Abd Manaf|عَبْد مَنَاف]],
so we have [[Qusayy ibn Kilab|قُصَيّ بن كِلَاب]], and we have his son [[Abd Manaf|عَبْد مَنَاف]]. Now [[Abd Manaf|عَبْد مَنَاف]], he had a number of sons as well.
[[Abd Manaf|عَبْد مَنَاف]] had [[Hashim|هَاشِم]] and he had [[al-Muttalib|الْمُطَّلِب]], and he had other sons as well.
Now the son of [[Hashim|هَاشِم]]
was a boy named [[Shaybah|شَيْبَة]].

So let's look at the generations here. We have [[Qusayy ibn Kilab|قُصَيّ بن كِلَاب]], and we have his son [[Abd Manaf|عَبْد مَنَاف]], and then we have his son [[Hashim|هَاشِم]], and then we have his son [[Shaybah|شَيْبَة]].
So [[Shaybah|شَيْبَة]] grew up
with his mother, because [[Hashim|هَاشِم]] died while [[Shaybah|شَيْبَة]] was still a young boy.
And the mother of [[Shaybah|شَيْبَة]] lived outside of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] actually. The mother of [[Shaybah|شَيْبَة]], she was from, her family was from
outside of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]]. So she kept her son with her outside of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]].
And the father of this boy, [[Hashim|هَاشِم]], had already died.
Now, when this boy grew up, when [[Shaybah|شَيْبَة]] grew up, when he became adolescent, when he reached maturity,

his uncle, [[al-Muttalib|الْمُطَّلِب]], and [[al-Muttalib|الْمُطَّلِب]] was another one of the sons of [[Abd Manaf|عَبْد مَنَاف]], and [[al-Muttalib|الْمُطَّلِب]] was the brother of [[Hashim|هَاشِم]].

So [[Hashim|هَاشِم]] passed away, and [[Hashim|هَاشِم]]'s son [[Shaybah|شَيْبَة]] is growing up with his mother outside of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]]. [[al-Muttalib|الْمُطَّلِب]] is still there in [[Makkah|مَكَّة]].
Now when [[Shaybah|شَيْبَة]] becomes mature, when he becomes an adolescent, his uncle [[al-Muttalib|الْمُطَّلِب]] comes from [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] to take the boy back to [[Makkah|مَكَّة]].
So he comes to the mother's house and says, 'I want to take my nephew, [[Shaybah|شَيْبَة]], back to [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] with me.'
And she said, 'No, how can you take my son away from me?'

And then [[al-Muttalib|الْمُطَّلِب]] said that, 'Your son, the son of my brother [[Hashim|هَاشِم]], he is a leader, and he cannot stay outside of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]]. He is from the leading family, and he needs to go back to [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] now that he has reached age.'

So the mother said, 'Okay, let's leave it in his choice. Let him do whatever he wants to do. Let the boy decide for himself. If he wants to stay with me, he can stay with me. If he wants to go with you, he can go with you.' So they gave the choice to [[Shaybah|شَيْبَة]].

And [[Shaybah|شَيْبَة]] said, 'I'm going to go back to [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] with my uncle, [[al-Muttalib|الْمُطَّلِب]].' Because he wanted to be part of that honor of leading [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] and taking care of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]]. He didn't want to just stay outside with his mother.
So he goes with his uncle [[al-Muttalib|الْمُطَّلِب]], and they enter back into [[Makkah|مَكَّة]].
Now, it was known those days that slavery was very common, and the people would go outside of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] and they would buy slaves and they would come back into [[Makkah|مَكَّة]].

So when [[al-Muttalib|الْمُطَّلِب]] came back with his nephew into [[Makkah|مَكَّة]]—and his nephew's name was [[Shaybah|شَيْبَة]]—when [[al-Muttalib|الْمُطَّلِب]] came back with his nephew [[Shaybah|شَيْبَة]] back into [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], the people see [[al-Muttalib|الْمُطَّلِب]] with this young boy, they don't know who he is, they think, 'Oh, [[al-Muttalib|الْمُطَّلِب]] has gone outside of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] to buy a slave, and he's bringing his slave back into [[Makkah|مَكَّة]].'

So they call this young boy, they say he is [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]]. He is [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]], the slave of [[al-Muttalib|الْمُطَّلِب]], even though that was not his name. His name was [[Shaybah|شَيْبَة]], but he became known as [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] because of that.
And [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]], as you know, he is the grandfather of [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ.

Now [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]], he had many sons. He had ten sons and he had six daughters. So he had sixteen children: ten sons and six daughters. And amongst his sons was the father of [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ, [[Abdullah ibn Abdul Muttalib|عبد الله]] [[ibn|بن]] [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]].

So now we can get an idea of the lineage of [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ a little bit, right? So we have [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ: [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] [[ibn|بن]] [[Abdullah ibn Abdul Muttalib|عبد الله]] [[ibn|بن]] [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] [[ibn|بن]] [[Hashim|هَاشِم]] [[ibn|بن]] [[Abd Manaf|عَبْد مَنَاف]] [[ibn|بن]] [[Qusayy ibn Kilab|قُصَي]] [[ibn|بن]] [[Kilab|كِلَاب]].

This is the lineage of [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ: [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] [[ibn|بن]] [[Abdullah ibn Abdul Muttalib|عبد الله]] [[ibn|بن]] [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] [[ibn|بن]] [[Hashim|هَاشِم]] [[ibn|بن]] [[Abd Manaf|عَبْد مَنَاف]] [[ibn|بن]] [[Qusayy ibn Kilab|قُصَي]] [[ibn|بن]] [[Kilab|كِلَاب]].

So [[insha'Allah|إن شاء الله]], next week we will talk about [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] and we will talk about how he rediscovered the well of [[Zamzam|زمزم]]. The well of [[Zamzam|زمزم]] was buried for centuries, and how, what is the story of [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] rediscovering that well. We will talk about that next week, [[insha'Allah|إن شاء الله]].

segments.translit: Wallahu a'lam, wa sallallahu wa sallama wa baraka 'ala nabiyyina Muhammadin wa 'ala alihi wa sahbihi ajma'in.
